To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a new SCLC antigen has been identified by MAb CR101.
a novel cell surface glycoprotein expressed by SCLCs is defined by a MAb, CR101.
CR101 recognizes an antigen that is associated with SCLCs, and that this antigen is composed of two proteins, 94 kD and 115 kDa, that are glycosylated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel SCLC marker that may be useful for the diagnosis and treatment of this disease.
the development of a novel antigenic marker associated with SCLCs.
the development of MAbs that recognize cell-surface antigens of SCLC.

CR101 recognizes a protein of 94 and/or 115 kD that is highly glycosylatied.
the antigen CR101 recognizes a novel protein expressed on SCLC cells.
the CR101 antigen is a glycoprotein with a molecular mass of 94-115 kD that is associated with SCLCs and may have a role in tumor progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CR101 recognizes a novel protein expressed in a subset of SCLC cell lines.
CR101 recognizes a novel SCLC-associated antigen that may prove useful in the development of new diagnostic and therapeutic modalities for the treatment of SCLC.
the CR101 antigen is a cell surface protein that is associated with small-cell lung cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CR101 is a novel SCLC antigen that may be used as a target for immunotherapy of this disease.

the MAb CR101 may be useful in the diagnosis and prognosis of patients with SCLC, as well as for the detection and characterization of SCLC cell lines.
